items.title: Lemaitre before Hubble
items.claim: Hubble's 1929 paper reported a relationship between galaxy distance and redshift, indicating expansion. Who derived the relationship two years earlier?
items.reveal:
Lemaitre's 1927 paper in Annales de la Societe Scientifique de Bruxelles included an estimate of the expansion rate.

The IAU resolved in 2018 to refer to the law as the Hubble-Lemaitre Law.
items.why: Language and journal of publication shape who gets credited for foundational results.

items.title: The first confirmed exoplanets
items.claim: The first exoplanets confirmed orbited an unusual host. What was it?

options.text: A pulsar (PSR B1257+12), with the discovery announced in 1992

items.reveal_title: Pulsar planets, three years before 51 Pegasi b
items.reveal:
Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail confirmed planets around the millisecond pulsar PSR B1257+12 in 1992.

Mayor and Queloz's 51 Pegasi b (1995) was the first around a sunlike star and won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.
items.why: Public memory often centres on the second discovery if the first occurs in an exotic setting.

items.title: Lunar samples returned
items.claim: How much lunar material did the six Apollo missions return to Earth in total?
items.reveal:
Apollo 11 returned about 22 kg; later missions returned larger samples. Soviet Luna robotic missions returned around 0.3 kg.

China's Chang'e 5 (2020) returned around 1.7 kg.
items.why: Sample-return missions remain extremely costly per gram delivered, shaping research priorities.
